products: KEIM Granital, KEIM Lignosil-Verano, KEIM Concretal-Lasur, KEIM Stucasol, KEIM Brillantputz, KEIM Innostar, KEIM Innotop, KEIM Silan-100, KEIM Klassik-MW
colours: Verano 4870 applied several times, render and paint KEIM Exclusiv 9310
story: In the midst of housing estates from the 1930s, an architect built his own home and an apartment building. The result is two buildings that at first glance look like settlement houses, but on the inside they have a modern and reduced design with a combination of wood and concrete. A special project that was also characterised by sustainability. The small town of Kandel in the southern Palatinate is only a few kilometres from the French border.

name: Residential House
sub: Nestled in a magnificent landscape, this dream house reflects the attitude to life of its builders.
story: How do you make a dream house come true? For example, like the Scholz-Neuner family from Pegnitz in Upper Franconia: on a south-facing slope, with a dedicated architect and mineral products from KEIMFARBEN. The first stroke of luck was the building site. It is located on a sunny south-facing slope in the middle of a miners' settlement from the 1950s and offers an unobstructed view of the city all the way to the Schlossberg with its striking lookout tower. Then the architect came into play: "In the design process, the client's wishes were central to us from the very beginning," explains Volker Schwab.

name: Hotel Miramonte
sub: Colour treatment for a former spa hotel
story: The owners of the Miramonte gave the hotel a special mix of 60s charm and modern design. Restored wooden elements, newly upholstered armchairs, design classics and specially made pieces characterise the hotel, which is constantly evolving – with colour as an important design element. When Evelyn and Ike Ikrath, she a hotel manager and passionate hostess, he an architect, acquired the Miramonte in 2008, they deliberately wanted to preserve its brittle 1960s charm: The floors were refurbished, wooden fixtures restored, chairs reupholstered and reupholstered.

name: Atrium House in Weiden
sub: This atrium house interlocks simple and clear architecture with nature in an impressive way.
story: The declared goal of sustainable building is to achieve high building quality while conserving existing resources. This means the construction of buildings that are ecological, economical in the long term and durable in terms of construction technology and building culture, with a high quality of life and living. Whether it is a new building or an old one - sustainable construction and renovation requires energy-efficient planning and the selection of durable, pollutant-free and disposal-friendly materials.

name: Luitpoldbad
sub: Where kings once bathed, there is still a special flair in the air today.
products: KEIM Biosil, KEIM Soliprim, KEIM Granital, KEIM Universalputz, KEIM Innostar, KEIM Unikristalat
architect: Gerhard Grellmann / Rainer Kriebel / Christian Teichmann
builder: Free State of Bavaria - Zentrum Staatbäder Bayern, Bad Steben
story: There is still a special ambience that reigns within the walls of the old historic rooms of bath "Luitpoldbad" in the German spa town in the Bavarian region of Lower Franconia "Bad Kissingen". It is a unique place where once kings and emperors took their bath. Even after decades of vacancy and extensive repairs, many historical areas of the building complex have retained their special atmosphere. The measures went hand in hand with the Office for the Preservation of Monuments and protected the building ensemble from deterioration. Today, the bathhouse serves as a workplace for public authorities.

name: Villa Carlotta
sub: The white wooden villa called "Carlotta" fits perfectly into a 1920s housing estate.
story: The timber-cladded villa in Erfurt's Steinhalde bears the name Carlotta - composed of syllables from the first names of the owners' twin daughters, Carla and Charlotta - and is a reminiscence of the previous owners' summerhouse. Steinhalde is a steep path that can only be accessed as far as Villa Carlotta.

name: Residential Complex Gossau
sub: Through its colourfulness, the object radiates values: Reliability and durability.
story: Discreetly coloured, pragmatic and car-free, this is how the new housing estate "Im Eich" in the Swiss municipality of Gossau in the Zurich Oberland presents itself. Cows and goats graze in the surrounding meadows, and yet Zurich's main railway station can be reached from here in just over half an hour. The nine buildings with a total of 87 rented flats follow the topography of the gently inclined slope at different levels, creating a configuration based around semi-public courtyards that have been arranged in a variety of ways.

name: Schweighof
sub: What has been implemented here in terms of craftsmanship will likely be preserved in over a hundred years.
story: What remains is Mount Pilatus, Kriens' local mountain. Otherwise, in the still young canyons of houses and street deserts between the village centres of Horw and Kriens, hardly anything reminds one of the former idyll close to Lake Lucerne. If it weren't for the Schweighof development, part of a new Lucerne urban quarter being built on 76,000 square metres. The natural landscape of the past, which has disappeared forever, is emblazoned on the northern façades of recently completed apartment buildings. The unusual façade design brings to the fore a craft that links past, present and future.

name: French International School
sub: Pedagogical innovation and the learning of the future becomes a reality in Henning Larsen's school.
builder: French International School of Hong Kong
story: In Hong Kong's Tseung Kwan O district, sunlight hits the kaleidoscopic facade of the new French International School campus and penetrates the building through windows laid over a grid of 627 colourful tiles. This puts the 19,600-square-metre new school, designed by Henning Larsen Architects, at the forefront of educational innovation in Hong Kong.

name: Hunters Point Library
sub: The Hunters Point Library in New York differs from its high-rise surroundings through shape and colour.
story: The team around Steven Holl can also build smaller formats: On the banks of the East River in New York, the architect’s office realised a slender, cuboid building that can hold 50,000 books and captivates with its silvery facade. Compared to the neighbouring residential towers of Queens, the new public library at Hunters Point seems almost tiny. Nevertheless: The only seven-storey high and extremely narrow building has become a landmark. The strict basic shape of a high cuboid is opened up by cut outs and organically shaped, freely arranged glass areas.

name: Schmuttertal-gymnasium
sub: The grammar school in Diedorf proves: Sustainability and pedagogy can be closely linked.
architect: Arge Hermann Kaufmann + Partner ZT GmbH und Florian Nagler Architekten GmbH
story: Around 1,000 pupils at the Schmuttertal Gymnasium learn according to innovative concepts in a healthy, meaningful environment. In a construction period of only two years, a plus-energy timber school building was created as part of a research project of the German Federal Foundation for the Environment, which breaks new ground: open learning landscapes that can be used in a variety of ways enable individual learning and teaching. The architecture not only meets the latest pedagogical requirements, but also the strictest ecological building standards.

notes: Completed in 2020.
story: Completed in 2020, the Royal Hobart Hospital in Tasmania's capital city Hobart is part of a new generation of hospital projects in Australia. The concept by Melbourne-based architectural firm Lyons Architecture follows the principles of salutogenesis. The facade of the state-of-the-art urban community hospital is closely interwoven with its surroundings. The design is characterised by soothing surfaces, colours, artwork and views – everything to ensure the well-being of everyone involved, including patients, their families and staff.

story: The new multi-storey ward building of the Joan Kirner Women's and Children's Hospital in Melbourne heralds a new approach to the design of healthcare facilities with its colourful façade. The new health-oriented design is intended to provide orientation for patients and visitors, increase well-being and reduce stress. Colour, design and architecture can support the healing of patients - this has been known for a long time. In Australia, the Joan Kirner Women's and Children's Hospital in Melbourne and the Royal Hobart Hospital in Tasmania's capital Hobart are two special hospitals.

name: St Leonard's College
sub: Tradition meets innovation hub
story: St Leonard's College in Brighton, a suburb of Melbourne, was founded in 1910 and combines historic and modern architecture. The campus includes the striking Heritage Building and modern extensions, including the Innovation Hub, newly built in 2020, which offers interactive learning spaces. These refurbishments enhance the learning environment and encourage creative approaches to education. St Leonard's is known for its strong academic programmes and offers an inspiring atmosphere that harmoniously combines tradition and innovation.

sub: Monumental bridge art by Glenn Hegedus for Main Roads WA
products: KEIM Concretal-Lasur, KEIM Faceal Oleo HD (anti-graffiti)
area: Thousands of m² of precast bridge abutments
notes: Main Roads WA changed its usual artwork policy to allow mineral paint here, and a second bridge project has already been approved with KEIM.
story: Along Albany Ring Road, artist Glenn Hegedus painted a series of bridge artworks drawn from the Great Southern’s rock formations, the coast of Princess Royal Harbour and stories shared on country with a Menang Noongar knowledge holder. Panels up to 9 metres tall were coloured with KEIM Concretal-Lasur, often through the night to beat the summer heat, giving the concrete a deep, flat, matte finish, then protected with KEIM Faceal Oleo HD anti-graffiti.

name: 201 Ellicott Street
sub: Affordable housing, fresh-food market and mobility hub with a mural by Josef Kristofoletti
story: A former surface car park on the edge of downtown Buffalo became 201 affordable apartments, a fresh-food market and the city’s first purpose-built mobility hub. Artist Josef Kristofoletti’s large mural is painted in KEIM Soldalit.

name: 166 Gertrude Street
story: 166 Gertrude is a six-storey boutique development by Melbourne developer Kalex, with 26 one-, two- and three-bedroom apartments over about 600 sqm of ground-floor retail on Gertrude Street, Fitzroy. Pre-sales opened in late 2015, construction was due to start in 2016, and completion was listed for around 2018. (The slug says Fitzroy North, but the address is in Fitzroy.)

name: Babworth House
story: Babworth House at 103 Darling Point Road is a heritage-listed mansion built in 1912-1915 for Sir Samuel Hordern, on the site of an earlier house by Mortimer Lewis with additions by Edmund Blacket. It later served as a hospital. After developers bought it in 2000, it was converted into luxury apartments and the gatehouse into a separate residence.

name: Elouera Tower
story: Elouera Tower is a 15-storey apartment and holiday-letting tower at 81 Sixth Avenue in the Cotton Tree area of Maroochydore, across the road from Maroochydore Beach. It has one-, two- and three-bedroom apartments and a three-bedroom penthouse, and levels 5 to 14 have uninterrupted ocean views.

name: Festival Towers
story: Festival Towers is a 41-floor, 135 m residential tower on the corner of Albert and Charlotte Streets in Brisbane's CBD, completed in August 2006. It was named after Brisbane's Festival Hall, which once stood on the site. Owner-occupiers, corporate short-stay guests and permanent renters now share the building.

name: Gallery of Modern Art (Millennium Arts Project)
architect: Architectus (GOMA); Donovan Hill with Peddle Thorp (State Library extension)
story: The Millennium Arts Project added two new public buildings to the Queensland Cultural Centre at South Brisbane: the Queensland Gallery of Modern Art (GOMA), designed by Architectus, and an extension to Robin Gibson's State Library of Queensland, designed by Donovan Hill with Peddle Thorp. Both were completed in 2006 and opened a week apart. The pin marks GOMA.

name: Newtown Silos (Crago Mill)
story: Newtown Silos is an adaptive reuse of the former Crago flour mill on Gladstone Street, Newtown. Its landmark grain silos were turned into three residential buildings with 59 apartments over 14 levels, with a metal-clad penthouse on top and a new low-rise building along Gladstone Street. The project ran from 1999 to 2005 and won awards in 2006. The coordinates are approximate (Gladstone Street).

name: Private residence, Elizabeth Bay
story: A residential project on Roslyn Gardens, a residential street running through Elizabeth Bay and Rushcutters Bay in Sydney's eastern suburbs. The old KEIM Australia gallery named only the street, so the exact building can't be identified and the suburb centre is used.

name: Silkwood Apartments
story: Silkwood is a mixed-use building in Surry Hills, on a former disused triangular site at the edge of the city. It has 48 apartments arranged around a courtyard, a 400-seat auditorium, and commercial and retail space, with upper levels mainly in precast concrete. It won the RAIA NSW Chapter Award for housing in 2007.

name: Stadium Australia (Telstra Stadium, now Accor Stadium)
architect: Bligh Lobb Sports Architecture (now BVN) with the Lobb Partnership (now Populous)
story: Stadium Australia was built for the Sydney 2000 Olympic and Paralympic Games, where it hosted the opening and closing ceremonies and the athletics. Its roof hangs from two large hyperbolic paraboloid trussed arches over the seating bowl. Its original 110,000 seats were reduced to about 80,000 after the Games, and it carried the Telstra Stadium name from 2002 to 2007.

name: UniLodge @ ANU (ANU Exchange student lodges)
story: UniLodge developed and manages four student residences (Kinloch, Davey, Warrumbul and Lena Karmel Lodges) in the ANU Exchange precinct between the ANU Acton campus and Civic. Kinloch Lodge stands on the former Childers Street Hall site, and Lena Karmel Lodge opened in 2012.

name: ABC Centre, East Perth
story: In 2005 the ABC moved its Perth operations from the 1960 studios on Adelaide Terrace into a newly built studio complex in East Perth, at Fielder Street near Claisebrook. The building houses ABC radio, television and newsroom operations for Western Australia.

name: State Library of South Australia (Mortlock Wing)
story: The State Library's original building on North Terrace, now the Mortlock Wing (called the Jervois Wing until 1965), was occupied in 1882 and formally opened in December 1884 as the second home of the South Australian Institute. It is a State Heritage Place, and its interior is one of the best-preserved Victorian libraries in Australia.

name: Royal Brisbane Hospital (Brisbane General Hospital Precinct)
story: The hospital opened on Bowen Bridge Road, Herston, in 1867, and by the end of the 1930s it was the largest hospital complex in Australia. Its historic precinct, which includes the 1875 Fever Ward and the 1895 Lady Norman Wing, was added to the Queensland Heritage Register in 2003.

name: Sydney Trades Hall
architect: John Smedley (original); Spain, Cosh and Minnett (additions)
story: Sydney Trades Hall, at 4-10 Goulburn Street on the corner of Dixon Street, is a Victorian Free Classical brick and sandstone building. Its foundation stone was laid in 1888, it opened in 1895, and it was extended up to 1916. Its octagonal corner tower has a copper cupola, and the building is on the NSW State Heritage Register.

name: ANZ Centre, Docklands
story: The ANZ Centre is ANZ's global headquarters at Docklands. It holds a workplace of about 83,000 m² for 6,000 people, organised around a central atrium, and ANZ moved its head office there from 2010. The project won the Emil Sodersten Award for Interior Architecture at the 2010 National Architecture Awards.

name: Atwell Buildings and Atwell Arcade
story: Atwell Arcade and the heritage-listed Atwell Buildings link High Street and Cantonment Street in Fremantle's West End. In a $13 million redevelopment of about 5,500 m², the upper floors became boutique offices and the original heritage features were kept.

name: Averi Apartments
story: Averi is a five-storey apartment building in Hawthorn East with 29 one- to three-bedroom homes over a semi-basement car park. It uses sculptural massing, clip-on 'lanterns' and layered landscaping instead of a stepped form, and Hutchinson Builders built it. It won an AIA Victorian Architecture Award for Multiple Housing.

name: Beaconsfield West Substation (TransGrid)
story: Beaconsfield West substation was commissioned in 1979 as the first major electricity supply point for inner Sydney. Around 2011-2012 TransGrid redeveloped it, adding a new building on each side of the existing substation, each housing 22 bays of 132 kV gas-insulated switchgear.

name: Broken Hill and District War Memorial
place: War Memorial Reserve, Argent & Sulphide Streets, Broken Hill
story: Sir John Monash unveiled the memorial on 11 October 1925. It is a Harcourt granite monument with a bronze soldier throwing a bomb, by Charles Web Gilbert, who died a week before the unveiling. Four bronze tablets carry the names of 365 men of the district killed in the Great War.

name: Charlestown Square
story: Charlestown Square is GPT Group's regional shopping centre in Lake Macquarie, near Newcastle. It opened in 1979, and a $470 million expansion finished in October 2010. It has about 93,400 m² of floor space on three levels and around 285 stores.

name: Children's Medical Research Institute (CMRI)
story: CMRI's research building on Hawkesbury Road, Westmead, is an eight-level facility with PC2 laboratories, tissue culture rooms, wet labs and a mass spectrometry facility. A W Edwards built it on a tight site within the Westmead hospital campus, and stage 1 was completed in 2014.

name: Common Ground Sydney
story: Common Ground Sydney is a 104-unit supportive housing building in Camperdown that brought New York's 'street to home' Common Ground model to Sydney, housing formerly homeless people alongside low-income tenants with 24-hour concierge and on-site support. It was designed by HASSELL and built by Grocon largely at cost for Housing NSW, targeting a 5-star Green Star rating, and was completed in 2011.

name: Dame Eadith Walker Estate (Yaralla)
architect: Edmund Blacket; additions by John Sulman
story: Yaralla, the Dame Eadith Walker Estate on the Parramatta River at Concord West, centres on an Italianate house built 1851-1864 for Thomas Walker to Edmund Blacket's design, with 1890s additions and stables by John Sulman. Dame Eadith Walker lived there until her death in 1937 and her bequest turned the estate into a convalescent hospital; it is now owned by NSW Health and its buildings house palliative care and dementia day-care services.

name: Flagstaff Green
story: Flagstaff Green is a residential development on Batman Street, West Melbourne, for Spec Property Group, with 242 apartments plus 25 serviced apartments, an indoor pool and gym. Designed by Peddle Thorp in brick, glass, timber and stone tile to sit comfortably beside its neighbours, it was completed in 2019.

name: Fremantle Prison
story: Fremantle Prison is a convict-built limestone prison constructed from the 1850s that operated until 1991 and is now a UNESCO World Heritage-listed site and visitor attraction. The WA Government has carried out ongoing conservation programs, including major works to the Main Cell Block, Commissariat and Parade Ground completed in 2023.

name: Glebe Incinerator
architect: Walter Burley Griffin and Eric Milton Nicholls
story: The Glebe Incinerator on the Blackwattle Bay foreshore at Forsyth Street was designed by Walter Burley Griffin and Eric Nicholls and built in 1933 as a municipal rubbish incinerator. Its sandstone D-shaped end has been restored and the flanking colonnaded sheds were reinterpreted in 2005, making it one of the best-preserved Griffin incinerators.

name: Glebe Town Hall
architect: Ambrose Thornley Jnr (original); Tonkin Zulaikha Greer (restoration)
story: Glebe Town Hall at 160 St Johns Road was designed by Ambrose Thornley Jnr and built in two stages in 1880 and 1891. The City of Sydney commissioned Tonkin Zulaikha Greer to restore it, and it reopened in March 2013; the failed exterior paint was stripped, the render remixed to match the original, and the facade repainted with breathable mineral silicate paint whose texture imitates stone.

name: Holiday Inn Sydney St Marys
story: Holiday Inn Sydney St Marys is a six-storey, 119-room hotel on the corner of Forrester and Boronia Roads beside the St Marys Rugby League Club, developed in partnership with IHG. Designed by WMK Architecture and built by FDC, it opened in late 2017/early 2018 with meeting rooms, a gym and a bronze-clad porte-cochere.

name: Santos Museum of Economic Botany
story: The Museum of Economic Botany in the Adelaide Botanic Garden opened on 27 May 1881 and is the last remaining museum of its kind in the world. Grieve Gillett Architects restored the interior and reinstated the 1880s layout, reopening it to the public in May 2009, with a second stage restoring the building exterior.

name: Newcastle Court House (former)
story: The former Newcastle Court House at 9 Church Street was designed by Colonial Architect James Barnet and built 1890-1892, with construction supervised by Walter Liberty Vernon. It closed as a court when the new Newcastle Justice Precinct opened in 2016 and was sold to Nihon University, which converted it into its Newcastle campus.

name: University of Newcastle Student Accommodation, Callaghan
story: John Holland built four eight-storey residential towers with 780 beds in 335 apartments on the University of Newcastle's Callaghan campus, finished in February 2015 for that year's intake. The project roughly doubled the university's on-campus student accommodation.

name: Orange Regional Museum
story: Orange Regional Museum at 151 Byng Street is a 1,300 m2 museum designed by Crone Architects, with a grassed roof that rises out of the existing civic lawn to form a public green space with views over the park and town. It opened in November 2016 as part of the civic precinct, with a civic square and amphitheatre seating, and has won architecture awards.

name: Parliament House, Western Australia
architect: John (Harry) Grainger (first stage); E.H. Van Mens (1964 extensions)
story: Parliament House on Harvest Terrace, West Perth, is the State Register-listed seat of the Parliament of Western Australia, built in stages from 1902 to 1978. Its first stage was designed by John Grainger and its 1964 extension, which created the current eastern facade, by E.H. Van Mens.

name: Pedare Christian College
story: Pedare Christian College is an independent Christian co-educational school in Golden Grove, in Adelaide's north-eastern suburbs. It appeared as a KEIM Australia reference project by 2016, listed for flooring work.

name: Private residence, Dalkeith
story: A private home on Victoria Avenue in the riverside Perth suburb of Dalkeith. It was listed as a KEIM Australia reference project by 2017.

name: Redfern Town Hall
story: Redfern Town Hall at 73 Pitt Street is an 1870 Victorian Regency sandstone civic building designed by George Allen Mansfield, seat of the Municipality of Redfern until 1948. South Sydney rugby league club was formed there in 1908, and Redfern Legal Centre has occupied it since 1977. It is heritage listed by the City of Sydney.

name: Federal Hotel (former Rosie O'Grady's)
story: The Federal Hotel at 23-25 William Street, Fremantle, opened on 1 July 1887 to a design by G.I. Inskip and was extended in 1904. It traded as Rosie O'Grady's Irish pub for about twenty years until January 2016, and later had the Federal Hotel name restored.

name: Clifton Views (TLC Aged Care)
story: Clifton Views on Queens Parade is TLC Healthcare's ten-storey residential aged care home with 127 suites and an integrated health hub, described as Melbourne's first high-rise aged care home. Built by Kane, it reached practical completion in Q3 2018.

name: UTS Yura Mudang student residence
story: Yura Mudang is the University of Technology Sydney's on-campus student residence in Ultimo, providing about 720 beds in studios and shared apartments with rooftop and communal facilities. It was built by Hutchinson Builders to a design by Nettletontribe.

name: Victorian College of the Arts Secondary School
story: The Victorian College of the Arts Secondary School is a select-entry government school for young dancers and musicians. Its purpose-built two-storey Miles Street facility of about 5,460 m2, designed by Williams Boag with sprung-floor dance studios and acoustic music rooms, was completed in June 2009.

name: Waurn Ponds Police and SES facility
story: A co-located Victoria Police station and State Emergency Service unit on Rossack Drive, Waurn Ponds, on Geelong's southern fringe, built in response to population growth with access to the Princes Highway. Accuraco project-managed the design, planning and construction for Victoria Police and the SES.

name: Wat Dhammadharo Thai Buddhist Temple
story: Wat Dhammadharo in Lyneham is Canberra's Thai Buddhist temple, whose 24 m pagoda in traditional Thai style is the tallest Thai Buddhist pagoda in Australia. Its columns, domes and details are glass reinforced concrete by Asurco Contracting, and the gold finish is a mineral paint chosen for durability and colourfastness.

name: Werribee Mercy Hospital
story: Werribee Mercy Hospital on the Princes Highway is the main public hospital for Melbourne's outer west, run by Mercy Health. It has had several expansions, including the four-level Stage 1C extension by Architectus with HDR completed in 2018.

name: Westmead Hospital
story: Westmead Hospital is a major public teaching hospital in Sydney's west and part of the Westmead health precinct. It was listed as a KEIM Australia reference project by 2015; the specific building painted is not documented.

name: Williamstown Town Hall
story: The former City of Williamstown Municipal Offices and Town Hall on Ferguson Street is an interwar civic building listed on the Victorian Heritage Register. It was refurbished by k20 Architecture in a project described as adding a further 100 years to the building's life, and it was shown as a KEIM Australia reference project.

name: Wynyard Walk
story: Wynyard Walk is a pedestrian tunnel and bridge link of about 180 m connecting Wynyard Station with Barangaroo and the western CBD. It was designed by Woods Bagot for Transport for NSW and opened in 2016. It was shown as a KEIM Australia reference project.

name: Private residence, North Bondi
story: A private home on Ramsgate Avenue in North Bondi, shown in the KEIM Australia project gallery. Its exterior was finished in KEIM mineral silicate paint.

name: Private residence, Paddington
story: A private home on Jersey Road in Paddington, a heritage suburb of Victorian terraces, shown in the KEIM Australia project gallery. It was finished in KEIM mineral silicate paint.

name: Cathedral of Christ the Saviour
story: The Russian Orthodox cathedral on the Moskva River was first completed in 1883, demolished in 1931 and rebuilt between 1995 and 2000. It is the tallest Orthodox church in the world, and KEIM listed it as one of its worldwide references.

name: CCTV Headquarters
story: The 234 m CCTV Headquarters in Beijing's Central Business District is a loop of two leaning towers joined at the base and at the top by a cantilevered bridge. It was designed by OMA with Arup engineering and completed in 2012, and KEIM listed it as one of its worldwide references.

name: Evelyn Grace Academy
story: Evelyn Grace Academy is a secondary school in Brixton run by the ARK academy trust, with a 100 m running track that passes through the middle of the building. Designed by Zaha Hadid Architects, it opened in 2010 and won the RIBA Stirling Prize in 2011. KEIM listed it as one of its worldwide references.

name: Grand Egyptian Museum
story: The Grand Egyptian Museum stands near the Giza pyramids and is the world's largest museum dedicated to ancient Egypt. It was built by a BESIX and Orascom joint venture and opened fully in November 2025. KEIM listed it as one of its worldwide references in 2015, while it was still under construction.

name: Private residence, Khyber Rock
story: A contemporary private home in Khyber Rock, a residential suburb of Sandton in northern Johannesburg. KEIM listed it as one of its worldwide references. The specific house and its architect could not be confirmed.

name: Linderhof Palace
story: Linderhof is the smallest of King Ludwig II of Bavaria's palaces and the only one he saw completed. It was built in the Rococo-revival style between 1874 and 1886 in the Graswang valley near Ettal. KEIM listed it as one of its worldwide references.

name: Mississippi State Capitol
story: The Beaux-Arts Mississippi State Capitol in Jackson was completed in 1903 and is the seat of the state legislature. It is a National Historic Landmark and has been restored several times. KEIM listed it as one of its worldwide references.

name: MuseumsQuartier Wien
architect: Ortner & Ortner (conversion); J. B. & J. E. Fischer von Erlach (original stables)
story: The MuseumsQuartier occupies the former Baroque imperial stables in Vienna's 7th district, combining the historic buildings with new museums such as the Leopold Museum and mumok. The conversion by Ortner & Ortner opened in 2001, making it one of the largest cultural complexes in the world. KEIM listed it as one of its worldwide references.

name: Old Grey Institute
story: The Old Grey Institute is a heritage-listed 19th-century school building in Port Elizabeth's historic Hill precinct, near Donkin Reserve. It was the original home of the Grey Institute, the school that grew into Grey High School. KEIM listed it as one of its worldwide references.

name: Royal Opera House
architect: E. M. Barry (1858); Dixon Jones (1999 redevelopment)
story: The Royal Opera House in Covent Garden is home to The Royal Opera and The Royal Ballet. The present theatre, designed by E. M. Barry, dates from 1858, and Dixon Jones carried out a major redevelopment completed in 1999. KEIM listed it as one of its worldwide references.

name: Run Run Shaw Creative Media Centre, City University of Hong Kong
story: The Run Run Shaw Creative Media Centre is City University of Hong Kong's faceted, crystalline media school building, with studios, theatres and labs. Designed by Daniel Libeskind, it was completed in 2011. KEIM listed it as one of its worldwide references.

name: Schwerin Castle
architect: Georg Adolf Demmler, Friedrich August Stüler (1845-1857 rebuild)
story: Schwerin Castle stands on an island in Lake Schwerin and was the residence of the Dukes and Grand Dukes of Mecklenburg. Its present Historicist form comes from a rebuild between 1845 and 1857, and today it houses the state parliament of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and a museum. KEIM listed it as one of its worldwide references.

name: Virginia State Capitol
architect: Thomas Jefferson with Charles-Louis Clerisseau; Hillier Architecture (2007 restoration)
story: Thomas Jefferson designed the Virginia State Capitol, modelled on the Roman Maison Carree, and it was completed in 1788. A major restoration and underground extension was completed in 2007 for the 400th anniversary of Jamestown. KEIM listed it as one of its worldwide references.

name: The Lucerne Hotel
place: Upper West Side, New York City
story: The Lucerne is a Beaux-Arts hotel built in 1904 at West 79th Street and Amsterdam Avenue, with an ornate brownstone and brick facade. It was designed by Harry B. Mulliken, and KEIM listed it as one of its worldwide references.

name: 3 Townhead
story: A Grade C listed mid-terrace cottage in the Kilmaurs conservation area had a peeling acrylic coating over lime render. The owner stripped it herself and then painted the cottage with KEIM Royalan, showing that a homeowner can apply the system.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: 7 St Helens Crescent
products: KEIM Soldalit-ME, KEIM Soldalit Grob, KEIM Fixativ, KEIM Innostar, KEIM Restauro Lasur
colours: Soldalit-ME 9197 and AG71 (exterior); Innostar 9314 + Restauro Lasur 9529 (walls); Innostar 9255 + Restauro Lasur 9249 (cornice)
story: Interiors stylist Charlie Davis renovated this double-fronted Victorian house as a hireable location house. A spare room got a limewash-look finish from KEIM Innostar layered with Restauro Lasur, and the lime-rendered exterior was repainted in KEIM Soldalit-ME.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Union Court
products: KEIM Restauro Lasur, KEIM Restauro Fixativ
story: GPAD Architects wanted to change the look of a plain yellow stock-brick workspace building without a film-forming coating. After site trials, only the brick faces were coloured with KEIM Restauro Lasur, leaving the mortar joints natural; one firm sprayed and the other hand-painted.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: 20 Farringdon Road
story: A tired 1980s granite-clad office block beside Farringdon station was given a bold black finish as part of a light-touch refurbishment for Derwent London. KEIM Royalan was applied directly to the abraded polished granite and protected with an anti-graffiti wax.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: 20 Heydon Road
colours: Stone colour to match front elevation
story: A brick village house with a rendered rear extension and a newly lime-rendered side wall was painted in KEIM Soldalit-ME. The colour was matched to the natural stone of the front so the render sits quietly against the brickwork.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: 27-29 Whitfield Street (Cyclone House)
products: KEIM Restauro Lasur, KEIM Restauro Fixativ
story: This former office building in the Charlotte Street conservation area was refurbished and extended, with old render stripped to reveal the brick. KEIM Restauro Lasur was chosen with the conservation officer so the brick would harmonise with neighbouring stone and a listed modernist building.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: 36 & 37 Hertford Street Residences
products: KEIM Soldalit, KEIM Soldalit Fixativ, KEIM Soldalit Grob
story: Two Georgian buildings in Shepherd Market were converted into 16 luxury apartments. The repaired lime-rendered facades were primed, evened out with Soldalit Grob and finished in a soft magnolia KEIM Soldalit.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: The Marshall Building, London School of Economics
products: KEIM Concretal Lasur, KEIM Concretal Fixativ
story: Grafton Architects' new LSE teaching building has a helical concrete stair and tree-like concrete columns in a tall internal hall. The fair-faced concrete was evened out and protected with KEIM Concretal Lasur while keeping its natural look; the building has won several awards.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: 46-47 Grange Walk
products: KEIM Restauro Lasur, KEIM Restauro Fixativ
story: Supply problems meant a new apartment building's extra brickwork did not match the original. KEIM's colourist built up several translucent layers of Restauro Lasur, including an algae-green tint, to make the new bricks read like weathered old ones.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: The Shoregate
products: KEIM Royalan, KEIM Royalan Grob, KEIM Royalan Dilution
story: A coastal restaurant with rooms in Crail's conservation area reopened after a 30-month restoration. The conservation officer recommended KEIM so one system could cover lime roughcast, cement, pebbledash and smooth render, with Royalan chosen for the harsh seaside weather.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Ackworth House
story: A landmark beachfront former nursing home in Filey was turned into eight apartments. The stripped stucco was re-rendered with fibre-reinforced KEIM Turado and finished in KEIM Royalan to stand up to the sea air.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Beechgrove
products: KEIM Design Lasur, KEIM Design Base
story: The owners of this private house wanted the painted concrete walls of their basement garage to look like bare concrete again. After the walls were dried out, KEIM Design Lasur was sponged on to recreate a natural concrete appearance.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Brilliant Botanicals Murals
story: Two public murals for the Brilliant Bamboo programme celebrate Stoke's ceramic heritage, one beside the canal and one near the former Spode works. The artists chose KEIM for its breathability on historic brick and its low environmental impact, adding KEIM metallic gold highlights.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Bryn Gwalia Hall
products: KEIM Royalan, KEIM Royalan Grob, KEIM Algicid, KEIM Spachtel
story: A 19th-century manor house in an exposed rural spot near Oswestry had its unpainted render cleaned of mould and repaired. It was then decorated with the KEIM Royalan system, a first KEIM job for the local decorator.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Bykenhillock
story: The owners of an old rubble-stone cottage in Glen Prosen compared limewash and KEIM side by side before choosing KEIM Royalan. Once the walls had dried out from repointing, the cottage was painted to look like traditional limewash but with a far longer life.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Café del Marsh
story: A Parisian-style café, wine bar and music venue on Lower Marsh was one of the first showcases for KEIM Colourwash. One coat of Colourwash BASE and one of the KNIT shade gave a soft limewash look over previously painted plaster.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: The Castle Hotel Windsor
story: This hotel opposite Windsor Guildhall began life as a 16th-century inn and later held royal warrants. During its restoration the old render was replaced with natural hydraulic lime and painted in photocatalytic KEIM Soldalit-ME.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Clare Priory
products: KEIM Soldalit-ME, KEIM Soldalit Fixativ, KEIM Soldalit Grob
story: Founded in 1248, the Grade I listed priory is one of England's oldest religious houses and is now a retreat. It was repainted in stages from 2017 in a traditional Suffolk Pink KEIM Soldalit-ME, chosen for resistance to algae under the surrounding trees.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Compass Community Hub
story: A former neighbourhood learning centre was rebuilt as a community hub with housing and training for young people. The new render on its wind-exposed elevations was painted in four colours of KEIM Royalan.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Crofton Lodge
products: KEIM Soldalit, KEIM Soldalit Fixativ, KEIM Algicid
story: A Grade II listed 19th-century house split into apartments was suffering damp and mould behind acrylic paint. The base was re-rendered in lime and the building repainted with KEIM Soldalit, which bonds to sound old paint while keeping as much breathability as possible.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Crow Leasow Farm B&B
story: The owners refurbished a Grade II* Jacobean and Georgian manor farmhouse in the Shropshire Hills as a guest house. KEIM's rep and colourist helped choose period-appropriate KEIM Optil colours for the interiors under a tight filming deadline.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Manhattan Apartments (Devonshire House)
story: A seven-storey loft-style apartment scheme off New York Street kept its red-brick facade but wanted an industrial blue-black look. A four-coat KEIM Restauro Lasur stain changed the brick colour without making it look painted.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Devonshire Row, 150 Bishopsgate
products: KEIM Fixativ, KEIM Soldalit, KEIM Restauro Lasur
colours: Soldalit 9295; Restauro Lasur ST019 and ST002
story: In this large mixed-use redevelopment, a retained Bath stone facade had to match the new Portland stone around it. KEIM Soldalit followed by two coats of Restauro Lasur blended the old stone into the new.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Domestic property in Cornwall
story: This seaside house was the first UK project to use KEIM Twinstar, a two-in-one wet-on-wet masonry paint. The painted stone gables were stripped first so the walls could breathe, and bare stone was treated with KEIM Lotexan.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Converted church home
story: The owner of a converted church in Leven repainted its tall interior on the advice of a church-restoration architect. KEIM Optil went straight onto the painted plaster, plasterboard and sandstone mullions without primer.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Dreel Halls
products: KEIM Royalan, KEIM Royalan Grob, KEIM Design Lasur, KEIM Silan Primer, KEIM Algicid
story: A community venue made up of an A-listed former church and C-listed former town hall sits in a salty, splash-prone roadside spot. After limewash failed within two years, it was redone with a KEIM Royalan system topped with Design Lasur.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Durbridge House
products: KEIM Universal Render, KEIM Royalan, KEIM Algicid
story: A 16th-century farmhouse near Gloucester was renovated after algae and flaking paint took hold. Damaged stone at the base was skimmed with KEIM Universal Render and the house finished in KEIM Royalan.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Ellenborough House
products: KEIM Soldalit-ME, KEIM Soldalit Grob, KEIM Spachtel
story: A Grade II listed Georgian facade joined to a 1970s-80s concrete office block was repainted for longevity at Cheltenham Borough Council's request. Repairs were filled with KEIM Spachtel and the whole facade finished in KEIM Soldalit-ME.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Islington 'Ugly Duckling' house
story: A quirky 1945 house built by a local postman on a wartime bomb site, among grand stucco terraces, was renovated and extended. The brick front and rendered base were painted in a warm white KEIM Soldalit so the old and new brick read as one.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Falkener House
story: A 17-storey 1968 council tower near Coventry city centre needed a facade coating with an A2-s1,d0 fire classification. After cleaning, it was repainted with KEIM Soldalit-ME, the first of several Coventry towers done this way.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Former farmhouse near Presteigne
products: KEIM Soldalit, KEIM Soldalit Fixativ, KEIM Algicid
story: A late 18th-century Grade II listed farmhouse in Powys had heavy algae on its limewashed stone. After cleaning and priming it was painted in KEIM Soldalit, recommended by a decorator who had used it on his own house.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Gracefield Parish Church
products: KEIM Optil, KEIM Optil Grob, KEIM Fixativ
story: A B2-listed church that began as a Moravian church in 1767 had cracking inside its distempered lime plaster. The surfaces were consolidated, evened out with Optil Grob and repainted in KEIM Optil.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Hampden House
story: This Grade I listed 16th-century country house in the Chilterns, now a wedding and events venue, was first painted in KEIM Granital in 2011. It was refreshed in 2025 with a bespoke-colour KEIM Soldalit-ME after lime render repairs.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: High Wray Bank
products: KEIM Universal Render, KEIM Mineralputz, KEIM Royalan
story: A Victorian country house overlooking Lake Windermere was restored with National Trust and Friends of the Lake District involvement. Stone and new blockwork were rendered with KEIM Universal Render and Mineralputz and finished in off-white KEIM Royalan.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: HMP Five Wells
applicator: D & A Decorators Northampton; T.O.L. Decorators
story: Britain's largest prison, a new category C rehabilitation jail, used KEIM after it had been applied at HMP Wrexham. Precast concrete on the housing, admin and medical blocks was cleaned and painted with KEIM Soldalit-ME for an even colour.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Holland House
products: KEIM Royalan, KEIM Royalan Grob, KEIM Restauro Lasur
story: The surviving east wing and arcades of this Grade I listed 17th-century house in Holland Park, now a youth hostel, were restored. A KEIM Royalan system with a Restauro Lasur glaze gave the west arcade a stone effect, and Royalan covered the soffits and east wing.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Jessamine Cottage
story: The owner first painted this thatched seaside cottage in KEIM Granital about 20 years earlier, with one refresh coat in between. In 2020 it was repainted in the same colour with KEIM Royalan because of the sea air, showing how long the system lasts.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Link Road Mural
story: Francis Gomila's 1982 street-scene mural had badly faded. Peterborough Presents and Nene Park Trust restored it with KEIM Soldalit, matched to the original colours, on the advice of Hirst Conservation.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Echo Building
story: Liverpool Echo's 18-storey 1974 brutalist tower on Old Hall Street was converted into a mixed-use building with a hotel and sky bar. Its exposed concrete panels were painted with KEIM Royalan for a sleek, long-lasting finish in an exposed spot.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Longhurst
story: New houses on the former Longhurst estate overlook the Lagan Valley. The architects used KEIM Granital on render and KEIM Concretal Lasur on smooth concrete; the scheme was shortlisted for the 2024 RSUA Awards.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Lower Peaches Farm
products: KEIM Granital, KEIM Granital Dilution, KEIM Algicid-Plus
story: Worn layers of limewash on lime roughcast were mostly removed from this Cotswold farmhouse. A two-coat KEIM Granital system replaced it, and the owners liked the front so much they did the rest of the house the next year.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Marina Park
story: An 1888 seafront residential building exposed to harsh coastal weather needed its painted render restored. After cleaning, a Soldalit Grob base and two coats of KEIM Soldalit-ME gave a breathable, durable finish.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Meadow House
story: A 17-storey 1967 block of flats in Coventry was the second tower in the city repainted with KEIM for fire safety. KEIM Soldalit-ME meets the A2-s1,d0 classification required on buildings over 18 m.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: National Flag Heritage Centre
products: KEIM Royalan, KEIM Royalan Dilution, KEIM Soldalit
story: A 1583 doocot behind Athelstaneford church, birthplace of the Saltire legend, houses the national flag museum. Its new lime render was coated with KEIM Royalan for exposure and topped with colour-matched KEIM Soldalit.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Arlington Court estate cottages (National Trust)
products: KEIM Soldalit-ME, KEIM Fixativ, KEIM Soldalit Grob, KEIM Algicid-Plus
story: Three homes on the National Trust's Arlington Court estate in Devon had limewashed render that kept growing algae. The Trust chose KEIM Soldalit-ME as a more resilient breathable finish.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: Newington Green Unitarian Church
story: London's oldest surviving nonconformist chapel, built in 1708 and Grade II listed, was renovated with Heritage Lottery funding. KEIM Optil was used on internal lime plaster and KEIM Soldalit-ME on the external lime render.
src: KEIM Mineral Paints UK case study

name: New Court, Trinity College
